title: Syncevid co-change mining report (Step 42)
description: Paths that changed in the same commits within an observation window, with Support, Confidence (+ a Wilson score interval) and Lift. Closed: every field the engine can emit is declared here, and nothing else validates. Every edge is tagged as temporal co-occurrence and not a dependency, on the edge itself, because a reader who slices one edge out of a report is exactly who the warning is for.

blake3Hex.description: Lowercase BLAKE3 hex. Uppercase would make two spellings of one digest.

ppm.description: Parts per million, integer arithmetic only: the exact counts beside it are authoritative and this rendering is for ordering and thresholding.

exclusionReason.description: Why a commit the history walk reached is not part of the mined population. The report carries non-zero counts only, and `commits_seen == commits_considered + sum(excluded)` holds by construction.

edgeClaim.description: One variant, on purpose. A boolean could be set wrong; an enum with one value cannot be omitted, misread, or defaulted into existence.

commits_considered.description: The population the ratios are over.

walk_truncated.description: Whether the committed bound stopped the walk before history ran out, in which case the window may be incomplete.

window_seconds.description: A duration, not a date. The window is anchored at the newest commit's timestamp read from the repository, never at a clock reading, so the same repository always yields the same window.

reference_oid.description: The commit the window is anchored to: content-addressed, so it carries no clock reading. Empty when the repository has no resolvable HEAD.

commit_set_digest.description: BLAKE3 over the considered commit ids. Timestamp-free by construction, and it pins exactly which commits the percentages are over.

coChangeEdge.description: One mined pair. `a` sorts before `b`, so the identity of an edge does not depend on which direction a reader asked about.

kind.description: The domain's own graph vocabulary, pinned so a co-change edge can never be read as `calls`.

lift_ppm.description: P(A and B) / (P(A)P(B)). Unbounded above: a rare pair that always travels together produces a very large number, which is exactly the number that must not be read as a dependency.

coverage.description: Per edge, because the measurement covering the population completely and this particular number resting on two commits are different statements.
